title_orig: Cribratio Alkorani (Cribrationis Alchoran), Liber III and prologue
date: c. 1460-61 (date given in the team brief; the scanned prologue is addressed to Pope Pius II, pontificate 1458-1464)
genre: Polemical treatise / refutation of the Qur'an (three books; dialogue-like apostrophes to Muhammad, to a 'Caliph of Baghdad', to a 'Sultan')
edition_original: Nicolai de Cusa Opera, 1565 printing as digitised by the Herzog August Bibliothek Wolfenbuettel (pages 914-931 read: image-01014 to image-01031; running head 'Cribrationis Alchoran', 'Liber III'); cross-checked against Haec accurata recognitio trium voluminum ... (Paris: ex officina Ascensiana, 1514), McGill digitisation, PDF pages 262-263 (prologue, 'Cribratio Alchoran'), 257 (De pace fidei). Printer of the 1565 volume not visible in pages read.
edition_english: No public-domain English translation found. Jasper Hopkins's translation (1990, in-copyright) was NOT quoted; no quote_en used for this work.
digital_url: https://archive.org/details/drucke_413-theol-2f_01014-01031 (item page; page images read at http://diglib.hab.de/drucke/413-theol-2f/start.htm?image=01014 to image=01031); 1514 print: https://archive.org/details/McGillLibrary-rbsc_heac_accvrata-recognito_folioBX890N4851514_v1-3-21741 (text-layer PDF read)
licence: archive.org item metadata: licenseurl https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/ (Public Domain Mark). HAB Wolfenbuettel terms on the scan: CC BY-SA 3.0 DE for the digitisation (attribution required); the 16th-century text itself is public domain.
authenticity_note: Genuine work of Nicholas of Cusa (no dispute found). Quotations of the Qur'an are Cusanus's own citations, using the Latin translation of Robert of Ketton (Cusanus's own statement in the prologue names a Latin translation procured through Peter of Cluny; read as printed 1514 prologue).
notes: Prologue (1514 print, PDF p.262): addressed to 'Pio secundo universalis christianorum ecclesiae summo ... pontifici'; Cusanus says he read the law of the Arabs in the Latin translation 'per Petrum abbatem cluniacensem' procured at Basel, and found an Arabic Qur'an with the Franciscans at Constantinople ('apud fratres minores ... apud sanctam crucem'). In the 1565 pages, Liber III, cap. XVIII is addressed 'Ad Caliphum de Baldach'. The chapter numbers of the Qur'an that Cusanus cites (e.g. 'cap. 17', 'cap. 70') are his own numbering; not checked against modern numbering.

date: 1453 (en.wikipedia: written shortly after the fall of Constantinople, 1453)
genre: Philosophical dialogue (heavenly council of representatives of nations and religions)
edition_original: Haec accurata recognitio trium voluminum ... Nicolai Cusae (Paris: ex officina Ascensiana, 1514), vol. 1, fol. CXXI (Dialogus, Cap. XIIII, speakers 'Alemannus' and 'Petrus'); PDF page 257 of the McGill text-layer copy.
edition_english: No public-domain English found (Lawrence Bond, Mellen 1991 facing Latin/English is in copyright and was NOT quoted).
digital_url: https://archive.org/details/McGillLibrary-rbsc_heac_accvrata-recognito_folioBX890N4851514_v1-3-21741 (PDF page 257 read as image and text)
licence: Paris 1514 print: public domain (16th century); McGill digitisation on archive.org (no licence field set in metadata read).
authenticity_note: Genuine (Cusanus). The Islam passage is spoken by the interlocutor 'Petrus' in the dialogue; not a quotation of another author.
notes: The Epistola ad Ioannem de Segobia (1454) was NOT found in the 1514 print (index checked; only the prologue to the Cribratio names Johannes de Segobia). Its Latin is printed in Klibansky-Bascour, Opera omnia vol. VII (1959), in copyright; not opened. The 1565 Basel neighbouring scans (drucke_413-theol-2f_00979-00982, 00983-00997, 00998-01013) returned HTTP 503 at download and were not read.

title_orig: Llibre del gentil e dels tres savis (Libre del gentil e los tres savis)
title_es: El libro del gentil y de los tres sabios
title_en: Book of the Gentile and the Three Wise Men
genre: Dialogue / philosophical novel (four books: Jew, Christian, Saracen, plus first book on God)
edition_original: Obres de Ramon Llull (1886) Palma edition as transcribed and proofread on Viquitexts (ca.wikisource), page numbers as in the Viquitexts index (Quart libre pp. 231-289). The Palma 1906- Obres (vols IX, XX) were consulted only for manuscript descriptions; their text of the Gentil was not used.
edition_english: No public-domain English translation read; English text NOT given (quote_en left empty; own_translation_en used).
licence: Viquitexts transcription: CC BY-SA (text page footer). Base 1886 edition: public domain (19th century).
authenticity_note: Genuine Llull (no dispute found in pages read). Passages attributed to the Saracen are the character's arguments, not Llull's own statements.
notes: Viquitexts footnotes ('Edit. lat.') give variants from a Latin version that was NOT identified or read. The Saracen's arguments in the Quart libre are presented without the Gentile's reply in the 'De l alcora' article as transcribed (see passage limits). The en.wikipedia summary says the Gentile converts to Christianity; the LeBlanc thesis says the reader never learns which faith the Gentile chooses (both read); the text of 'De la fi d aqvest libre' read names no religion in the part read.

title_orig: Liber disputationis Raimundi christiani et Homeri saraceni
title_es: Disputa de Raimundo cristiano y Homero sarraceno
title_en: Book of the Dispute of Raymond the Christian and Omar the Saracen
date: 1308, Pisa (per en.wikipedia and LeBlanc 2023 thesis section 6; written from memory after a shipwreck)
genre: Recorded debate (report of a disputation with a Muslim scholar)
edition_original: NOT OPENED. Modern critical edition: Aloisius Madre, ROL XXII / CCCM 114, Brepols 1998, pp. 172-264 (cited in LeBlanc 2023 bibliography; in copyright). Old print: 1510 edition listed on Google Books (id thc4CxBjXWwC); the Google Books API returned HTTP 429 and the book was not read.
edition_english: Not read. (en.wikipedia links a Spanish blog translation; not opened.)
digital_url: Not read. Google Books id thc4CxBjXWwC (1510 print) listed on en.wikipedia; API call rate-limited.
licence: Not determined (1510 print would be public domain; not reached).
authenticity_note: Not assessed beyond secondary sources (LeBlanc 2023 thesis; en.wikipedia).
notes: No passage from this work is included in passages.json: the Latin text was not opened. Secondary reading only: LeBlanc 2023 thesis (read at https://www.ub.edu/llulldb/docs/LEBLANC%20Disputatio%20Raimundi%20et%20Homeri.pdf) states the Disputatio is more 'vitriolic' than the Llibre del gentil and that the Saracen's arguments against the Trinity are 'Umar's; this is a secondary characterisation.
